channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Stranded locals use rare truce to leave Moscow-occupied town in Ukraine
item.description: Some residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine ravaged by food and medicine shortages, left on Friday during a rare ceasefire brokered by the United States – due to end on Sunday evening. Ukrainian and Russian officials visited the town together on Friday, delivering aid and marshalling those who wanted to leave.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump's weekend rallies in Kansas, Iowa are back on
item.description: The rallies were cancelled on Thursday.

item.title: Comey's attorneys return to court to fight DOJ's efforts to charge him for 3rd time
item.description: Attorneys for ex-FBI Director James Comey are expected to ask a judge to dismiss new criminal allegations that accuse him of mishandling classified information in 2016.

item.title: ICE officer who struck man with vehicle during pursuit indicted: DA
item.description: The officer, Mario Alberto Morales, was charged with second-degree aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, according to the Harris County District Attorney's Office.

item.title: WATCH: What we know about Binance security breach
item.description: Dave Merkel, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity company Expel, talks about the major breach.

item.title: Star Wars: Has Russia's war with Ukraine gone intergalactic?
item.description: Russian made an unprecedented combative move this month as one of its military satellites, the Cosmos-2612, encroached upon the orbit of Ukrainian commercial satellite, Iceye-X36, in behaviour deemed "threatening" by the US State Department. Norbert Pouzin, an orbital analyst at French space tech firm, Aldoria, described the mercenary manoeuvre as the first of its kind.

item.title: Could US midterms impact the EU? Transatlantic ties hit new low after Trump-Putin diesel deal
item.description: From the EU's perspective, the second Trump presidency has felt even more destabilising than the first. From making the false claim that the EU was set up to "screw" the United States, to slapping tariffs on European goods, to making territorial claims on Greenland, to doing a diesel deal with Vladimir Putin and telling Ukraine to get a new president, Donald Trump has more than ruffled feathers on this side of the ocean. He has shaken the very foundations of the historical transatlantic relationship.

item.title: French port strikes: Unions 'will get better working conditions', but can they curb militarisation?
item.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. An international dockworkers’ strike brings into focus the relationship between organized labor, technological change and Europe’s expanding military investment. Foucart argues that port workers’ strategic position in global supply chains gives them exceptional leverage: “They know how powerful they are.” While questioning their ability to redirect military policy, he expects that leverage to secure concessions on automation and working conditions: “They can get those concessions. And I think they will get them.”

item.title: War in Ukraine: Evacuations under way in Russian-occupied Oleshky
item.description: Starving and exhausted residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine, were being evacuated on Friday, October 30, as part of a joint relief operation involving the opposing sides – the first operation of its kind in four years and eight months of war. FRANCE 24’s Ukraine correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze reports.

item.title: French crowd gathers for anti-islamophobia rally in Paris suburb after attack
item.description: In France, thousands were protesting in the Paris suburb of La Verrière on Friday, a week after a racist terrorist attack killed one person and injured five others. The suspect, identified as Kevin T., admitted he was targeting people based on their appearance or religion and has been transferred to a Paris court. FRANCE 24's Morgan Ayre reports.

item.title: WATCH: State of the race with 4 days until midterm vote
item.description: Nearly 45 million people have already turned out to vote, and those early voting numbers have surpassed where the numbers were at this point in the 2022 midterm election.

item.title: Biggest hack in history: Cryptocurrency giant Binance loses $6.3 billion
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange giant Binance has been targeted by a record-breaking $6.3 billion cyber heist, with blockchain intelligence firms linking the attack to North Korea. By Thursday night in the US, a coordinated effort by major crypto platforms successfully froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen assets during a high-stakes race to track and secure the digital funds.

item.title: Spain working to identify train crash dead as relatives' anguish grows
item.description: A second day of mourning is underway in Spain, with some families still waiting for news about missing loved ones, following Wednesday's high speed train crash that killed 69 people. Some have flooded social media with desperate appeals for information, posting photos or describing the clothes their relatives were wearing when they boarded the trains.

item.title: Midterms 2026: The former neo-Nazi pastor speaking out against Trump
item.description: According to one poll, 82 per cent of white evangelical Protestants voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 US presidential election. That makes pastor Caleb Campbell a significant outlier – he has been one of the few outspoken evangelical critics of the Trump administration, dating back to the president’s first term when he felt compelled to speak out against Trump’s plans to put “kids in cages” as part of an immigration crackdown. “I was told that I was possessed by a demon,” Campbell remembers. Now, as the midterms approach, he fears US politics and the current administration have become more distant than ever from the Bible’s teachings.

item.title: Israeli election: 'Netanyahu did not win, he lost dramatically,' former PM Barak says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "did not win" this week's election in Israel but "lost dramatically", and that his rival Gadi Eisenkot should ally with Arab parties. Barak also suggested that claims of Qatari funding for an Arab party aimed to distract from an ongoing corruption scandal, and warned that Netanyahu was ready to strike Iran to stay in power.

item.title: 'Deeply hurt': Convicted murderer Christa Pike speaks out after botched execution
item.description: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike said she remains in constant pain after surviving a botched lethal injection in September, in her first public statement since the failed execution. She expressed gratitude for those who saved her life while urging compassion for her victim's family.

item.title: Former non-league football club boss admits offences linked to rape of woman drugged by husband
item.description: The former chief executive of a non-league football club has admitted offences linked to the rape of a woman who was drugged by her husband.

item.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock as final results show no clear winner
item.description: Israel's wartime election appeared deadlocked on Tuesday, exit polls showed, ​with Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc running neck and neck with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, leaving neither side with a clear path to power. The projections pointed to a setback for Netanyahu's coalition and potentially weeks of political wrangling to form a government. FRANCE 24's Jerusalem correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky has more.

item.title: NPR special: 5 takeaways from a year of listening to swing voters
item.description: Every election, there is a crucial sliver of voters who help determine which candidates win. Here are five takeaways from a year of listening to voters who backed Biden in 2020 and then Trump in 2024. (Image credit: Ryan Murphy)

item.title: Bugatti CEO chases chases down car thief - then offers him lift home
item.description: The head of the luxury car-maker Bugatti has promised to stop leaving his keys in his own car after his £2m model was stolen from a company site in Zagreb.

item.title: France braces for new wave of protests, govt warns of 'very high' violence risk
item.description: France's interior minister on Thursday warned of a "very high risk of public disorder" and announced the deployment of around 70,000 police officers for a new wave of protests this weekend. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more.

item.title: Billionaire tax, transgender rights, voter access among key midterm ballot measures
item.description: Voters will weigh in on several key ballot measures in the midterm elections.

item.title: Black Sea shipping under growing threats as drones hit container ships
item.description: A Greek container ship has sunk after being struck by three drones, potentially of Russian origin, in the Black Sea off the Bulgarian coast on Wednesday, October 28. This incident highlights growing concerns for commercial shipping as the conflict between Ukraine and Russia persists.

item.title: 'The Phantom of the Opera' haunts French cinemas again
item.description: In this edition of arts24, "Le Fantôme de l'Opéra" returns to French cinemas in a contemporary reinterpretation starring Deva Cassel and Romain Duris. We take a closer look.

item.title: Spanish transport minister faces calls to quit after deadly train crash
item.description: Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente faced calls to resign but ruled out stepping down on Friday. This follows Wednesday’s train crash in Toledo province, which killed 69 people. It is the country’s second high-speed rail disaster this year. FRANCE 24 correspondent Sarah Morris reports.

item.title: Third weekend of protests looms as tensions persist across France
item.description: For the third Saturday in a row, people across France are set to take to the streets to protest against the high cost of living and demand better funding for education. Police are preparing for all eventualities ahead of another weekend of protests, following earlier demonstrations that ended in rioting and looting in city centres.

item.title: Who is Kevin T., the main suspect behind the racist Trappes attack?
item.description: France's anti-terrorism prosecutor on Thursday released details of the main suspect in the racist attack in Trappes and La Verriere, on the outskirts of Paris, on October 23.The 39-year-old opened fire with a submachine gun, killing 26-year-old Pengo Bossio Wangi and injuring five others.

item.title: How will the women's vote shape the US midterms?
item.description: With the US midterms approaching, we examine the power of the women's vote in an election that will shape the balance of power in Washington during Donald Trump’s final two years in office. Annette Young talks to Annie Karni, congressional correspondent for The New York Times and Kelly Dittmar, Director of Research at the Centre for American Women and Politics.

item.title: How the record-breaking $6.3 billion heist in crypto history unfolded
item.description: Hackers stole $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance in a record-breaking heist, prompting issuers to freeze roughly half of the stolen assets. The breach, which US analysts suspect was done by North Korean hackers, has shaken confidence in the crypto market.

item.title: Georgia's European dream left in limbo
item.description: Two years ago in Georgia, tens of thousands of pro-European protesters rallied against the disputed results of the October 2024 parliamentary election, which was officially won by the ruling Georgian Dream party. A few weeks later, the authorities announced the suspension of the country's European Union accession process. Despite an ongoing crackdown, smaller-scale protests continue every day in the capital Tbilisi.

item.title: Texas Republicans accused of changing electoral rules ahead of midterms
item.description: With the US midterm elections approaching, Republicans in Texas are being accused of changing electoral rules in their favour. In Tarrant County, near Dallas, they've cut the number of election-day polling places by nearly 30 percent. The decision is being challenged in court and adds to last year's state-wide redistricting, a move designed to benefit Republicans. But the measures could also help galvanise the Democratic opposition. FRANCE 24's Pierrick Leurent reports, with Wassim Cornet.

item.title: Dem wants to keep Trump from buying DC golf course after federally funded renovations
item.description: Rep. Huffman wants "guardrails" to keep the president from profiting from it.

item.title: ‘Scared of crossing the border’: The Arizona farmers who rely on Mexican workers
item.description: The vast produce farms of Yuma County, Arizona, rely heavily on foreign workers who cross the border every day from Mexico. John Boelts, a farmer and staunch supporter of US President Donald Trump, praises the administration’s strict border controls – though he says that competing Republican factions have complicated efforts to hire foreign labourers.

item.title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after company given lowest environmental rating
item.description: Yorkshire Water has announced its chief executive is stepping down - a day after the company was given the lowest environmental rating by regulators.

item.title: DOJ issues grand jury subpoenas to election officials in California
item.description: DOJ issues grand jury subpoenas to local election officials in California as part of its investigation into the state’s voter rolls, multiple sources told ABC News.

item.title: Trump administration says biggest changes coming to infant formula in nearly 30 years
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration announced on Thursday it is proposing a new rule that will update the nutrient requirements for infant formula.

item.title: DOJ issues new wave of subpoenas in criminal probe of Alaska Senate race, sources say
item.description: The DOJ is issuing new subpoenas in a probe of Alaska's U.S. Senate race and alleged efforts by Democrats to recruit a candidate with the same name as the GOP incumbent.

item.title: Why is the Cheesecake Factory at the center of the latest culture war?
item.description: A joke by former President Obama has gone viral and received backlash from the Trump administration as the issue of affordability looms large over next week's midterm elections. (Image credit: Kayla Bartkowski)

item.title: AI-powered 'doorbell cameras' tested to alert people to approaching polar bears
item.description: Artificial intelligence-powered "doorbell cameras" are being tested by a team of international experts in Canada to warn communities about approaching polar bears as climate change increases the risk of dangerous encounters.

item.title: Banished: The Taliban's War On Women - tickets go live for Sky News documentary screening
item.description: Tickets are now on sale for a screening, followed by a Q&A, of Alex Crawford's new documentary, Banished: The Taliban's War On Women.

item.description: Homes have been evacuated while a bomb squad examines "several suspicious items" found by police after a row between neighbours.

item.description: Some passengers sold their home to live on the cruise ship full-time.

item.description: As tributes pour in for Sir Patrick Stewart, World News Tonight remembers his interview with Diane Sawyer – sharing how theater became his safe space and his home.

item.title: Democrats seek to weaken the Republican lead in state legislatures
item.description: Republicans control 10 more state legislatures than Democrats. That's where most laws on taxes, abortion, crime and schools are made. (Image credit: Aimee Dilger)

item.title: For voters from immigrant families and new citizens, voting is bigger than themselves
item.description: While many young voters are focused on the cost of living in the election, for some from immigrant families, the political calculation — and their votes — is often about even more than the economy. (Image credit: Courtesy of Nicole Solis-Sison)

item.description: The competitive map for control of the U.S. Senate has expanded considerably in the final days before Election Day. Here's a ranking of those competitive races from most likely to flip to least likely. (Image credit: Megan Varner)

item.description: Profits at the UK-based oil and gas giant BP have hit an 18-year high, surpassing the level seen during the 2022 energy crisis.

item.title: Vote Republican, or else: How Trump is dangling government help on the campaign trail
item.description: President Donald Trump is signaling to states that his administration may be far less likely to help if their voters put Democrats in power on Election Day

item.title: Police investigating Andrew's Balmoral stays with Epstein and Maxwell
item.description: Police are investigating Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's stays with Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell at the Royal Family's private estate in Scotland.

item.description: Cryptocurrency worth more than $6.3bn (£4.7bn) has been stolen from a major exchange - with one industry insider telling Sky News it is "the largest bank heist in human history".

item.description: ABC News’ Devin Dwyer reports on the issues voters are weighing, and Cynthia Cox, senior vice president and director of KFF’s Program on the Affordable Care Act, discusses the ACA.

item.description: The former president took issue with how President Donald Trump responded to his joke about "the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory."

item.title: FIFA to double Women's World Cup prize money - but it doesn't match men's tournament
item.description: FIFA plans to double Women's World Cup prize money next year but will not deliver on Gianni Infantino's ambition to match the cash paid out at the men's tournament, Sky News has learnt.

item.title: Watchdog investigating Met Police over handling of letter about Meghan's father
item.description: The Metropolitan Police is being investigated by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) over a letter containing allegations about the Duchess of Sussex's father, Thomas Markle Snr.

item.description: Shares in Google's parent company Alphabet have suffered their worst-ever day on the US stock market, falling more than 12% and knocking around half a trillion dollars off its value.

item.description: Sky News has obtained copies of leaflets promoting medical clinics in illegal Israeli settlements by a company seeking to recruit British Jewish doctors at an event in London

item.title: Why defeated Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Miami - and what comes next
item.description: On Wednesday, Flavio Bolsonaro, who last week lost Brazil's presidential election, was seen arriving in the US on a private jet after having fled in the dead of night.

item.title: WATCH: Maine’s loggers and fishermen speak up about tariffs and higher diesel costs
item.description: ABC News’ Jay O’Brien talks to Maine Senate candidates Troy Jackson (D) and Sen. Susan Collins (R), as well as to fishermen and loggers impacted by tariffs placed on machinery imported from Canada.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family from Maine that makes sure their yard always has a leaf pile ready for their two leaf-loving dogs.

item.description: A small crowd took to the streets of Boston to protest against the existence of Liberty Biberty, the new fuzzy yellow mascot that appears in the insurance giant Liberty Mutual's TV ads.

item.description: ABC News’ Linsey Davis speaks with a Long Island couple suing a now-former broker at realtor Douglas Elliman for housing discrimination, after the broker sent a text saying “Ugh they are black.”
